subject: Sidecar bundle lifecycle, discount & rollback
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@neurolytics.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@neurolytics.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify 'sidecar' bundle — upgrade vs add-on?

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal readout and two follow-ups came up from product/ops: is the Sidecar feature (low-latency routing + local KV cache) treated as a separate add-on we can buy without changing our existing tier, or does enabling Sidecar require a tier upgrade? The distinction matters for pricing and for how we think about rollback if the pilot doesn't meet latency targets.

Quick context: we expect ~8–12M tokens/month steady state, with short bursts up to 30M/month for a few days. We can share the current traffic profile if that helps.

Can you send the current pricing constructs (per-sidecar billing, any minimums, upgrade equivalence) and what rollback/stepdown looks like if we want to revert after the pilot?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if needed.

Best,
Alex
Product Lead — Neurolytics
Attachments: usage_snapshot_sep2026.csv (referenced)

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify 'sidecar' bundle — upgrade vs add-on?

Hi Alex — thanks for the context, this is a good question. Short answer: Sidecar can be purchased as an add-on for your existing tier or as part of a committed tier upgrade. Below are the tradeoffs and the rollback path. I'm attaching a concise pricing_summary_v3.xlsx with numbers.

1) Add-on path (recommended for a pilot)
- Billing: per-active-sidecar-hour + small per-sidecar token uplift. No permanent tier change.
- Minimums: 200 sidecar-hours/month for pilot pricing.
- Discount: for a 6-month pilot we can apply an 8% usage discount tied only to sidecar charges; for a 12-month commit we can extend to 12% (applies to both sidecar hours and incremental tokens).
- Rollback: we support a same-day disable; final billing reconciles to actual usage with a 30-day refund window for unused pre-purchased sidecar-hours if you choose to stop.

2) Tier upgrade (recommended if you expect steady higher throughput)
- Billing: moves you to the next tier (higher reserved capacity) with lower per-token unit cost and includes Sidecar as part of the capacity bundle.
- Discounts: upgrades carry standard commit discounts (tiered). We can anchor an additional 5% concession for an annual commit tied to the deal.
- Rollback: rolling back a tier requires a 30-day notice and prorated adjustment; we can structure a short canary period before commit to avoid heavy rollback exposure.

Operational notes:
- We recommend you start with the add-on pilot for 4–8 weeks to validate latency improvements. If steady-state token demand grows beyond your pilot sizing, we’ll run a capacity cost comparison and recommend the upgrade path.
- We'll expose canary monitoring in the Console (per-route latency + token delta) so you have objective criteria for rollback decisions.

Next steps I propose:
- I share the pricing spreadsheet (attached) with a recommended pilot configuration and estimated monthly cost range based on your usage snapshot.
- If that looks ok, we’ll draft an amendment (MCPA redline) for the pilot term and the discount schedule.

Would you like me to draft the pilot MCPA and a simple mutual action plan, or prefer a quick call to finalize sizing first?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_summary_v3.xlsx, sidecar_feature_matrix.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@neurolytics.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify 'sidecar' bundle — upgrade vs add-on?

Alex — quick thought from a deal-ops perspective. We like the add-on pilot route (low friction), but to reduce churn risk on our side we usually put a canary discount cadence in place:

- Pilot: 8% off sidecar usage for 6 weeks.
- If KPIs are met (latency SLO + <3% error/regression on quality metrics) we step to a 10% discount for months 2–6.
- For a firm annual commit we can add another 2–4% on top depending on total committed tokens.

If Neurolytics prefers an upgrade, offer: 5% one-time onboarding credit + 7% annual commit discount (negotiable).

I'll let Logan and Marissa handle the exact pricing math in the attached sheet, but happy to sync if you want to lock the cadence.

—Ben
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify 'sidecar' bundle — upgrade vs add-on?

Thanks Logan & Ben — this is helpful.

We want to proceed with the add-on pilot with the canary discount cadence you suggested. Confirming the asks so we have a single source of truth:

- Pilot term: 6 weeks (start on provisioning date)
- Minimum: 200 sidecar-hours/month (we expect to be under this early but ok to start here)
- Discount cadence: 8% for weeks 1–6, if KPIs met then 10% for months 2–6 of pilot (per Ben's note)
- Rollback: ability to disable same-day and receive reconciliation within 30 days for unused prepaid hours
- Deliverables from Redwood: pricing_summary_v3.xlsx (received), MCPA redline + short mutual action plan doc, and Console access to the canary dashboard

Could you send the MCPA redline and the mutual action plan (1 page) so procurement can review? If you can get that to me by EOD Monday we’ll aim to sign and kick the pilot on Tuesday.

I'll attach a quick note from procurement asking for standard liability language and data locality confirmation — looping Sarah for that.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Alex
Product Lead — Neurolytics
